documents.unit: Office of Academic Affairs (Instructional Faculty Academic Policy Manual; Academic Integrity Policy)
documents.title: Kean University Instructional Faculty Academic Policy Manual and Resource Guide, Fall 2025: Expectations of Generative AI
documents.date_or_term: Fall 2025 (AI text from the Academic Integrity Policy, Fall 2024 revision)
documents.stance_why: The text says "faculty members specify in their course syllabi how AI and GenAI may be used" and "guidelines may vary from course to course." The university sets only floor rules (originality, citation, integrity, consequences) and hands the stance to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: Kean's Academic Integrity Policy text, reproduced in the faculty manual, sets four universal rules (originality, citation, integrity, consequences) and lets each instructor set course-specific AI use in the syllabus. The manual adds guidance for faculty on deciding how much AI to permit, using several kinds of evidence, and talking with students.

units.why: Defines GenAI as software that generates content and names tools ("ChatGPT, GPT 4, DALL-E, Quillbot"), which sets what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: Generative AI (GenAI) includes programs such as ChatGPT, GPT 4, DALL-E, Quillbot, Vertex

units.why: "faculty members specify in their course syllabi how AI and GenAI may be used" leaves the rule to each instructor, so P04 (who decides), not P09 (duty to state).
units.anchor: faculty members specify in their course syllabi how AI and GenAI may be used
units.frag_start: At Kean University, faculty members specify
units.frag_end: may vary from course to course.
units.policy: Faculty members specify in their course syllabi how AI and GenAI may be used in their classes; guidelines may vary from course to course.

units.why: "Students are required to adhere to the specific requirements outlined in each syllabus" binds students to the course-level rule; each syllabus governs its own course, so P11.
units.anchor: Students are required to adhere to the specific requirements outlined in each syllabus.

units.why: "Content created by Generative AI cannot be presented as original student work" is a universal ban on passing off AI output as own work, so P19.
units.anchor: Content created by Generative AI cannot be presented as original student work.

units.why: "any content generated by AI must be cited and attributed" where AI is permitted is a duty to cite AI use, so P24.
units.anchor: any content generated by AI must be cited and attributed just like ideas
units.frag_start: Citation and Attribution: In courses where
units.policy: In courses where AI use is permitted, any content generated by AI must be cited and attributed just like ideas, text, speech, or imagery from human authors.

units.why: The form of attribution ("quotation marks, citations, and other forms of attribution") must separate student work from generated material. It names no tool, prompt or date, so P24 not P25.
units.anchor: attribution to clearly distinguish between the student's original work and material generated by external sources
units.frag_start: This includes the use of quotation
units.policy: Attribution includes quotation marks, citations, and other forms of attribution to clearly distinguish between the student's original work and material generated by external sources.

units.why: "Students are accountable for any content they create or publish" makes students responsible for what they submit, so P29.
units.anchor: Students are accountable for any content they create or publish.

units.why: "AI- generated content can be inaccurate, misleading, fabricated" warns that output is unreliable, so P31 (accuracy) rather than P53.
units.anchor: AI- generated content can be inaccurate, misleading, fabricated
units.policy: AI-generated content can be inaccurate, misleading, fabricated (referred to as hallucinations), or include copyrighted material.

units.why: "students must meticulously review all AI-generated content" is a duty to verify output and own its accuracy, so P31.
units.anchor: students must meticulously review all AI-generated content
units.frag_end: accuracy of any work they submit.
units.policy: If faculty policy permits the use of AI, students must meticulously review all AI-generated content, acknowledging their responsibility for the accuracy of any work they submit.

units.why: "or include copyrighted material" names a separate copyright risk of AI output, coded P52 apart from the accuracy warning.
units.anchor: or include copyrighted material
units.policy: AI-generated content can include copyrighted material.

units.why: "Faculty may use various tools and methods ... AI detection tools integrated into Canvas" lets faculty use detectors and comparisons as evidence, so P40, not P39.
units.anchor: AI detection tools integrated into Canvas
units.frag_start: Faculty may use various tools and
units.policy: Faculty may use various tools and methods to ensure appropriate use of AI, including comparisons with in-class or other written work and AI detection tools integrated into Canvas.

units.why: "demonstrated mastery of learning via the ability to orally present/discuss content" checks understanding by having students explain work, so P34.
units.anchor: demonstrated mastery of learning via the ability to orally present/discuss content
units.frag_start: Faculty may use various tools and
units.policy: Faculty may use demonstrated mastery of learning via the ability to orally present/discuss content to ensure appropriate use of AI.

units.why: "Use contrary to the course policy and/or without proper acknowledgement is subject to the same rules and consequences outlined for integrity violations" classifies misuse as an integrity violation, so P36.
units.anchor: without proper acknowledgement is subject to the same rules and consequences outlined for integrity violations

units.why: "failing the assignment, failing the course, and/or further disciplinary actions" lists concrete possible penalties, so P37.
units.anchor: inappropriate use may include failing the assignment, failing the course, and/or further disciplinary actions
units.policy: Consequences of inappropriate use may include failing the assignment, failing the course, and/or further disciplinary actions as per the University's academic integrity policy.

units.why: "supporting students as they learn to appropriately navigate key life tools, such as Artificial Intelligence" frames AI competence as a life skill, closest to P44.
units.anchor: supporting students as they learn to appropriately navigate key life tools, such as Artificial Intelligence
units.frag_start: Kean is committed to student success
units.policy: Kean is committed to supporting students as they learn to appropriately navigate key life tools, such as Artificial Intelligence.

units.why: "Students are encouraged to use student academic support services ... to avoid reliance on Generative AI tools" discourages reliance without forbidding AI, so P03.
units.anchor: to develop their skills and avoid reliance on Generative AI tools
units.policy: Students are encouraged to use student academic support services available at Kean to develop their skills and avoid reliance on Generative AI tools.

units.why: "Students uncertain about AI use expectations ... should seek clarification from their instructors" is the ask-first rule, P10.
units.anchor: Students uncertain about AI use expectations in a course should seek clarification

units.why: "Failure to seek clarification is not an acceptable excuse" makes not asking no defense in integrity cases. It belongs with the ask-first rule (P10), not P36, which is about classifying misuse.
units.anchor: Failure to seek clarification is not an acceptable excuse to challenge an academic integrity violation

units.why: "faculty are encouraged to clearly define their course-specific expectations for AI use in their syllabi" asks instructors to state AI expectations in syllabi and assignments (encouraged, so should), P09.
units.anchor: faculty are encouraged to clearly define their course-specific expectations for AI use
units.frag_end: should or should not utilize AI.
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to clearly define their course-specific expectations for AI use in their syllabi and on individual assignments, specifying how students should or should not utilize AI.

units.why: "Faculty should familiarize themselves with how artificial intelligence (AI) is used in their respective fields" asks instructors to learn about AI before setting expectations, so P63.
units.anchor: Faculty should familiarize themselves with how artificial intelligence (AI) is used

units.why: "the amount of generative AI use you allow in your class depends on your course objectives" says allowance is set per course by the instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: generative AI use you allow in your class depends on your course objectives
units.policy: The amount of generative AI use faculty allow depends on course objectives, the skills students should develop, and the role AI can play in enhancing or undermining those goals.

units.why: "Some tasks, such as drafting or generating ideas, might benefit from AI tools, while others ... should rely solely on the student's work" sorts tasks into AI-ok and AI-free categories, so P05.
units.anchor: others, like final analyses or personal reflections, should rely solely on the student's work
units.frag_end: rely solely on the student's work.
units.policy: Some tasks, such as drafting or generating ideas, might benefit from AI tools, while others, like final analyses or personal reflections, should rely solely on the student's work.

units.why: "Establish boundaries for when and how AI can be used in your class" tells each instructor to set the boundaries, so P04.
units.anchor: Establish boundaries for when and how AI can be used in your class.

units.why: "Require students to disclose when and how they use AI in their work" recommends that instructors require disclosure, so P24.
units.anchor: Require students to disclose when and how they use AI in their work.

units.why: "Help students understand the ethical implications of using AI, including issues of originality, plagiarism, and intellectual honesty" is ethics guidance, closest to P53.
units.anchor: Help students understand the ethical implications of using AI, including issues of originality

units.why: "the use of these tools remains a learning aid rather than a shortcut" gives the learning rationale for disclosure, so P41.
units.anchor: ensures that the use of these tools remains a learning aid rather than a shortcut

units.why: "start with a moderate approach, allowing limited use in low-stakes assignments" recommends limited AI first to observe its impact, which is staged permission, so P08.
units.anchor: start with a moderate approach, allowing limited use in low -stakes assignments
units.policy: It is reasonable to start with a moderate approach, allowing limited use in low-stakes assignments to observe its impact.

units.why: "Use this experience to refine your policy as you learn what works best" asks instructors to revise their policy over time, so P54.
units.anchor: Use this experience to refine your policy as you learn what works best

units.why: "faculty are encouraged to rely on multiple sources of information" including "AI detection tools" tells faculty to use varied evidence of misuse, so P40.
units.anchor: faculty are encouraged to rely on multiple sources of information
units.frag_start: When addressing potential academic misuse of
units.policy: When addressing potential academic misuse of AI, faculty are encouraged to rely on multiple sources of information, such as comparisons with other work, AI detection tools, and verbal demonstration of mastery.

units.why: "engaging students in open discussions about their work and the role AI played or did not play" asks faculty to talk with students about suspected misuse, so P57.
units.anchor: engaging students in open discussions about their work and the role AI played
units.frag_start: Equally important to this data is
units.policy: Faculty should engage students in open discussions about their work and the role AI played or did not play.

units.why: "guides students toward ethical and effective use of AI" states that those conversations teach effective AI use, so P44.
units.anchor: guides students toward ethical and effective use of AI
units.policy: Conversations can clarify expectations, uncover misunderstandings and guide students toward ethical and effective use of AI while reinforcing academic integrity and accountability.

units.why: "Faculty can decide to permit students to access support (such as ... AI, etc.) when working on take-home assignments/exams" leaves it to faculty, so P04.
units.anchor: Faculty can decide to permit students to access support
units.policy: Faculty can decide to permit students to access support, including AI, when working on take-home assignments/exams.

units.why: "Remember to indicate your expectations on the syllabus and/or individual assignment" tells instructors to state expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: Remember to indicate your expectations on the syllabus and/or individual assignment.

notes: Single manual section. No school or computing documents found.
